name: Cimarron River Pipeline Cimarron Expansion Project

values.StartLocation: Beaver Compressor Station area, Beaver County
values.EndLocation: National Helium Gas Processing Plant, Seward County

researcher_notes: A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice from December 2017 (docket PF17-7-000) says Cimarron River Pipeline LLC planned about 49.3 miles of new pipe in Beaver County, Oklahoma and Seward County, Kansas, plus a lease of 19.1 miles of an idle 26 inch line. New pipe is 20 inch (23 miles) and 30 inch (about 24.3 miles plus short laterals to the National Helium Gas Processing Plant). Added capacity is up to 631 million cubic feet per day. This is a new row in the expansion shape under the existing Cimarron River Gas Pipeline (P6900), which has no row for this project. The EIA project table for August 2026 (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 1148) lists it as an expansion by DCP Midstream, 48 miles, 631 MMcf/d, cancelled July 2018 because the anchor shipper withdrew. Status is cancelled on that source alone, so tier is medium. EIA and the notice are not independent for the capacity. Cancelled type and diameter (20 and 30 inch, mixed) were left blank. No route was found, and no cost was found. The EIA lists DCP Midstream as the sponsor, while the notice names Cimarron River Pipeline LLC, so the owner is a question for the ownership team.
